kings1.19.p1.b1.text: Now Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.

kings1.19.p1.b2.text: “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the lives of those you killed!”

kings1.19.p1.b3.text: And Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there,

kings1.19.p2.b1.text: while he himself traveled on a day’s journey into the wilderness.

kings1.19.p2.b2.text: He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die.

kings1.19.p2.b3.text: “I have had enough, LORD… Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.”

kings1.19.p3.b2.text: “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you.”

kings1.19.p3.b3.text: So he got up and ate and drank. And strengthened by that food, he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.

kings1.19.p4.b1.text: There Elijah entered a cave and spent the night.

kings1.19.p4.b3.text: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts… but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword…”

kings1.19.p4.b4.text: “…I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”

kings1.19.p5.b1.text: “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.”

kings1.19.p5.b2.text: And a great and mighty wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind.

kings1.19.p5.b3.text: After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire.

kings1.19.p5.b4.text: And after the fire came a still, small voice.

kings1.19.p6.b1.text: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave.

kings1.19.p6.b2.text: Suddenly a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

kings1.19.p6.b3.text: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts… I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”

kings1.19.p7.b1.text: “Go back by the way you came, and go to the Desert of Damascus. When you arrive, you are to anoint Hazael as king over Aram.”

kings1.19.p7.b2.text: You are also to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to succeed you as prophet.

kings1.19.p7.b3.text: Nevertheless, I have reserved seven thousand in Israel—all whose knees have not bowed to Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him.”

kings1.19.p8.b1.text: So Elijah departed and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve teams of oxen, and he was with the twelfth team.

kings1.19.p8.b2.text: Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak around him.

kings1.19.p8.b3.text: “Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you.”

kings1.19.p8.b4.text: “Go on back… for what have I done to you?”

kings1.19.p8.b5.text: So Elisha turned back from him, took his pair of oxen, and slaughtered them. With the oxen’s equipment, he cooked the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out to follow and serve Elijah.
